## Requirements: WebSocket Runtime V2 — reserved Stream execution capacity independent of Request admission

### Owner decision and scope
Follow-up to the post-implementation review of #4431/#4433/#4435, at main f527399914c03448aa8e4bb8909d211b52d6e4b3. Owner's original explicit decision: Control, Request and real-time data must be independently dispatched. The review on #4435 explicitly leaves a reserved input lane as a product design decision. This issue resolves that decision: the stream window alone is not execution isolation; implement separately reserved Stream execution admission. Historical issues are evidence and complementary owners only, not hard prerequisites; do not reopen/rewrite them or their past acceptance.

### Verified source evidence
- [P2P route table](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/f527399914c03448aa8e4bb8909d211b52d6e4b3/crates/nession-agent/src/server/websocket.rs#L3005-L3072): terminal input, resize and legacy applied operations declare Key(session_named).
- [Reader](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/f527399914c03448aa8e4bb8909d211b52d6e4b3/crates/nession-agent/src/server/websocket.rs#L4267-L4323): Key routes share ordinary lanes.try_key admission.
- [Lanes::shared](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/f527399914c03448aa8e4bb8909d211b52d6e4b3/crates/nession-runtime/src/lane.rs#L1326-L1384): one mutation-slot semaphore per connection, shared resource scheduler. A connection exhausting ordinary mutation slots can refuse independent terminal input despite the finite Stream window.
- #4435 post-review https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/issues/4435#issuecomment-7151627754 records this tension. No fresh runtime repro claimed here.

### Design
- Provide provider-declared Control/Request/Stream dispatch metadata orthogonal to wire category and FIFO resource policy, with one reader/writer per socket. Use the existing route ownership and generic runtime mechanism; do not add a parallel registry or peer-chosen priorities.
- Real Stream admission has its own reserved count/byte execution budget; ordinary Request saturation cannot consume it. Control keeps its own reserved progress path. Bound both process and connection scopes; a stream cannot monopolize another stream or the runtime. Preserve per-session order, generation/lease/epoch/frontier semantics and dependency fences at the Session owner. A genuinely conflicting same-resource mutation may fence stream activity; unrelated slow work must not.
- Treat input, output, progress, resize and state by provider semantic policy, not string prefix. Keep existing reliable input protocol, explicit overflow and recovery, no blind side-effect replay or false ACK. Avoid silent loss for legacy clients; use compatible explicit failure/recovery, version changes only if consumer-visible contract changes.
- Keep existing #4435 ownership of slow-observer fan-out, #4499 incarnation coalescence and #4500 issued-frontier validation separate; #4433 owns existing reader/control waits and inbound budget remediation. Develop against current adapter seam and test independently, integrate once shared runtime improvements land.
- Update canonical architecture route inventory and knowledge delta; a verified design is not proof of delivered runtime.

### Success Criteria
- [ ] SC-01 Under an exact-head barrier-controlled protocol integration test, fill ordinary mutation admission with unrelated slow operations on one P2P connection, then send terminal input/resize/progress on an attached independent session; valid stream work completes before releasing the request barrier, with correct ordered input bytes and no duplicate write. Negative fixture saturates only Stream and proves explicit bounded refusal and continued control/request progress.
- [ ] SC-02 The source-aligned staging Case proves the same saturated request/active stream/control overlap through both P2P and Relay in a single scenario per transport, using private tmux, configured small limits, measured concurrent events and teardown; stale generation/lease and conflicting kill/recreate are fenced without bypassing the Session owner.
- [ ] SC-03 Exact-head route coverage verifies all served real-time operations are explicitly assigned provider-owned stream/control/request policy and independent admission; unknown or malformed routes cannot consume reserved capacity; queue and active task bounds settle after disconnect.

SC → scenario: SC-01 SCN-03 (exact PR-head executed targeted CI/Gate/test evidence read by Agent); SC-02 SCN-03 (source-aligned staging protocol/runtime Case with authenticated exact SHA/Run/Attempt); SC-03 SCN-01 (exact PR-head executed targeted CI/Gate/test evidence read by Agent). PR CI tests must assert the decisive observable predicate, not merely presence of helpers. Runtime Cases use the existing approved isolated full-stack-local runner with private tmux and bounded fault injection, no privileged/production credentials. No blanket Full E2E.
